practical_skills: Filing to claim a refund of withholding

sections.skill: Decide whether to file, choose a filing status, and explain dependency

questions.prompt: Kayla earned $3,000, and $180 of federal income tax was withheld. Her income is below the filing requirement. Why might she file anyway?

choices.text: Because the IRS fines everyone who does not file
To get the $180 of withheld tax back as a refund

questions.correct_answer: To get the $180 of withheld tax back as a refund
questions.intro: Whether you must file depends on your income, filing status, age, and whether someone can claim you as a dependent. Even if you are not required to file, filing can get you a refund of tax that was withheld.
questions.feedback: Filing lets her claim a refund of the $180 withheld.
questions.topic: Filing requirements, filing status, and dependents
sources: IRS (Interactive Tax Assistant: Do I need to file?): Filing requirements depend on income, filing status, age, and dependency; people may file to get a refund of withheld tax even when not required. (https://www.irs.gov/help/ita/do-i-need-to-file-a-tax-return)

questions.prompt: Which filing status fits an unmarried person with no dependents?
questions.intro: Filing status affects tax brackets and the standard deduction. Statuses include single, married filing jointly, married filing separately, head of household, and qualifying surviving spouse.
questions.feedback: An unmarried person with no dependents files as single.
questions.topic: Filing requirements, filing status, and dependents

misconceptions.B: Requires a qualifying person and paying most household costs
misconceptions.C: Requires a deceased spouse and dependent child

questions.prompt: Jordan, 17, lives with his parents, who pay most of his support. What does it usually mean that his parents can claim him as a dependent?

choices.text: Jordan cannot file a return at all
They may get tax benefits for him, and he checks that he can be claimed on his own return
Jordan's wages are added to his parents' W-2

questions.correct_answer: They may get tax benefits for him, and he checks that he can be claimed on his own return
questions.intro: A dependent is a person, such as a child, whom another taxpayer can claim. Dependents can still file their own returns (for example, to get a refund). They indicate that someone can claim them, and their standard deduction may be limited, often based on their earned income up to a yearly cap.
questions.feedback: Dependents can file, but they must note that someone can claim them.

questions.intro: Married couples can file jointly (one return together) or separately. Joint filing usually results in lower combined tax.

sections.relationship: Filing decisions depend on knowing what a tax return does.

questions.prompt: What does filing a tax return do?

choices.text: It pays a fixed fee to the IRS
It calculates the year's tax and settles up with what was paid
It pays the year's tax for the first time
It is required only to get a refund

questions.correct_answer: It calculates the year's tax and settles up with what was paid
questions.intro: A tax return reports income, figures the tax owed for the year, and compares it with what was already paid (withholding), resulting in a refund or a balance due.
questions.feedback: The return settles the year's tax.

sections.skill: Head of household and other statuses

questions.prompt: Rosa is unmarried, pays more than half the cost of keeping up a home, and her son lives with her. Which status may she qualify for?
questions.intro: Head of household is for unmarried taxpayers who pay more than half the cost of a home for themselves and a qualifying person. It has a larger standard deduction and wider brackets than single.
questions.feedback: She meets the main tests for head of household.

questions.prompt: How does filing status affect the calculation of the final tax on a federal return?

choices.text: It sets the standard deduction and tax brackets used
It sets the employer's pay rate
It changes which forms the employer uses
It has no effect on the tax calculation

questions.correct_answer: It sets the standard deduction and tax brackets used
questions.intro: Each filing status has its own standard deduction and bracket thresholds, which are used to figure the tax on the return. (A W-4 also asks for a status, but that only sets withholding during the year.)
questions.feedback: Status changes the deduction and brackets, and so the tax.

questions.prompt: A dependent's standard deduction is limited when they can be claimed by someone else. For this scenario, assume it equals the greater of $1,350 or earned income plus $450 (up to $15,000). Kayla earned $3,000. What is her standard deduction?
questions.intro: A dependent's standard deduction may be limited, often to earned income plus a small amount, up to the regular cap. Some dependents with enough earnings reach the same cap as anyone else. Amounts change yearly; these are stated for this scenario.
questions.feedback: $3,000 + $450 = $3,450, which is more than $1,350 and less than $15,000.

questions.prompt: Kayla earned $3,000 and her standard deduction is $3,450. What is her taxable income?
questions.intro: Taxable income = income − deductions, but never below zero.
questions.feedback: $3,000 − $3,450 is below zero, so taxable income is $0.

questions.prompt: With $0 taxable income, what federal income tax does Kayla owe, and what happens to the $180 withheld?

choices.text: $0 owed; she can get the $180 back by filing
$0 owed, and the $180 that was withheld is lost

questions.correct_answer: $0 owed; she can get the $180 back by filing
questions.intro: Withholding counts as tax already paid. If the tax owed is $0, the withheld amount can be refunded when you file.
questions.feedback: No tax is owed, so the full $180 withheld is refunded when she files.

questions.prompt: Kayla owes $0 of federal income tax this year, but Social Security and Medicare (FICA) taxes were withheld from her $3,000 of wages. Are those FICA taxes refunded when she files?

choices.text: Yes, always, along with any income tax withheld
No; FICA taxes are not refunded just because income tax is $0
Only if she asks her employer

questions.correct_answer: No; FICA taxes are not refunded just because income tax is $0
questions.intro: FICA (Social Security and Medicare) taxes are separate from income tax. Owing no income tax does not make them refundable; only income tax that was withheld beyond what is owed comes back.
questions.feedback: FICA is separate from income tax and is not refunded because income tax is $0.
